lines: Avery Brooks
+1 (555) 010-3319 | avery.brooks@example.com | example.com/in/abrooks
Date of birth: 9 Jan 1998 | Nationality: Brazilian
EDUCATION
Eastmoor University | B.S. in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Riverside Cinema | Box Office Attendant | Metro City, USA | Aug 2025 - Present
- Sold tickets and concessions during evening shifts and balanced the cash drawer at close.
- Trained 3 new attendants on the ticketing system and the refund policy.
Brightcart Retail | Data Analyst | Metro City, USA | Aug 2022 - Jun 2025
- Built the weekly retention dashboard for 2.4M customers that marketing used to retarget lapsed buyers, lifting 90-day repeat purchase from 22% to 27%.
- Cut the monthly revenue report from 3 days of spreadsheet work to 2 hours by moving it to scheduled SQL queries and a shared dashboard.
- Found customers with no orders by left-joining the orders table to the customers table and counting rows with a null customer name.

- Joining 40 source tables, deduplicating customer records across two loyalty systems and rebuilding the attribution logic in dbt-style SQL models, raised the share of orders tied to a campaign from 58% to 81%.
- Presented the quarterly customer review to the leadership team, and two of its three recommendations were funded in the next budget.
- Trained 20 merchandisers to answer their own questions with the self-serve dashboards, halving ad hoc data requests.
Pinecrest Insurance | Junior Analyst | Metro City, USA | Jul 2020 - Jul 2022
- Ran the checkout A/B test until significance by checking the p-value every day and stopping on the first day it fell below 0.05.
- Analyzed 18 months of call-center data; my findings moved two agents to the evening peak and cut average hold time from 9 to 5 minutes.
- Writes the team's SQL style guide and review checklist, which cut query errors found in review by half.

- Automated the monthly fraud-flag extract while also maintaining the team calendar, answering ad hoc questions from sales, updating onboarding documents and covering the help desk on Fridays, which saved the fraud team 10 hours a month.
PROJECTS
City Bike-Share Demand Study | Independent Project | Python, SQL | Jan 2025 - Present
- Modeled hourly bike-share demand for 120 stations from 2 years of public trip data, forecasting next-day demand within 12% mean absolute error.
- Cut empty-station hours from 300 to 200 a week, a 50% reduction, in a replay of last summer's rebalancing.
- Raised forecast hit rate by 15% across 120 stations, from 60% to 75%, by adding weather and event features.
Food Pantry Visit Analysis | Volunteer, Team of 3 | Excel, SQL | Mar 2023 - Aug 2023
- Mapped 14 months of pantry visits by hour and day, so the pantry moved one volunteer shift and cut the Saturday line from 50 to 20 minutes.
- Cleaned 9,000 handwritten visit logs into a single table and matched repeat visitors, giving the pantry its first count of unique households.
- Wrote a one-page guide the pantry coordinator used to update the visit table each month after the project ended.
SKILLS
Tools: SQL, Python, Excel
Methods: dashboards, forecasting, metric design, data-quality checks

items.says: Make the LinkedIn URL clickable.
Add your current city and state or country near the contact details.
items.because: It helps when applying to location-specific roles.

items.says: Add a portfolio, GitHub, or project link if you have one.
items.because: A portfolio showing project methods and results may be especially useful for a data analyst résumé.

items.says: Remove the date of birth.
items.because: It is not relevant to your qualifications and can introduce bias.

items.says: Remove the nationality unless an application asks for it.
items.because: If work authorization matters, state that directly instead.

items.says: Trim routine shift detail if you need space.
items.because: It is less relevant to analyst roles than the rest of the experience.

items.says: Clarify whether the retention increase was attributable to the campaign or merely observed after launch.
items.because: The meaning of “lifting” is unclear.

items.says: Give a defensible comparison period or measurement basis for the retention increase.
Make the dashboard’s audience or recurring use apparent if there is room.
Correct the join direction used to find customers with no orders.
items.because: A left join from orders to customers would not normally identify them.

items.says: Do not rely on a null customer name to count customers with no orders.
items.because: Names could be missing for other reasons.

items.says: Describe the finding’s value or follow-up, if any.
items.because: The bullet explains a query technique but not its impact.

items.says: Fix the sentence fragment.
items.because: The action/result relationship is hard to follow.

items.says: Clarify whether you personally joined the tables.
Clarify what “dbt-style” means and whether you used dbt itself.
items.because: SQL models with a similar approach are not the same as using the tool.

items.says: Explain how the attribution change was measured.
Make the increase from 58% to 81% easier to spot.
items.because: It is a valuable result.

items.says: Clarify the nature or importance of the funded recommendations.
items.because: “Two of three” leaves their impact unclear.

items.says: State how and over what period the halving of ad hoc requests was measured.
Correct the described A/B testing method.
items.because: Checking the p-value daily and stopping below 0.05 can inflate the false-positive rate.

items.says: Include the test’s outcome or business decision if available.
Clarify whether the hold-time reduction was observed after the staffing change and over what period.
Change “Writes” to the appropriate past tense.
items.because: It conflicts with the past-tense bullets and the role’s end date.

items.says: Clarify the time period or basis for the reduction in review errors.
Separate or trim the unrelated duties.
items.because: The long list obscures the fraud automation and its impact.

items.says: Clarify what the ten hours saved represent and who benefited.
Use the actual project end date if the work is finished.
items.because: “Present” fits only if you are still maintaining or extending the project.

items.says: Identify the forecast error metric precisely.
items.because: “Within 12% mean absolute error” is ambiguous, and mean absolute error is usually expressed in the demand measure’s units.

items.says: Explain how the forecast was validated.
Correct the claimed 50% reduction.
items.because: A drop from 300 to 200 is a one-third reduction.

items.says: Make clear that the reduction came from a replay or backtest.
items.because: Readers might mistake a simulated result for an operational outcome.

items.says: Define “forecast hit rate” and distinguish it from the first bullet’s error metric.
Correct or qualify the claimed 15% increase.
items.because: Going from 60% to 75% is a 15-percentage-point increase or a 25% relative increase.

items.says: Clarify whether the line-time reduction was measured after the shift change and over what period.
Briefly explain the repeat-visitor matching method or privacy safeguards if relevant.
Add relevant tools you can use confidently, particularly BI platforms, databases, and analytics or statistical libraries.
items.because: The tools list is too limited for many data analyst postings.

items.says: Replace broad method categories with specific analytical capabilities you can perform.
items.because: The listed methods do not clearly distinguish skills such as forecasting, experimentation, and metric definition.

items.says: Group skills by category.
items.because: Recruiters and ATS can scan them more quickly.
